intro.title: Book Introduction - Romans
intro.html:
Book Introduction - Romans

WRITER: The Apostle Paul (Rom 1:1).

DATE: Romans, the sixth in chronological order of Paul’s Epistles, was written from Corinth during the apostle’s third visit to that city. 2Co 13:1 in A.D. 60. The Epistle has its occasion in the intention of the apostle soon to visit Rome. Naturally, he would wish to announce before his coming the distinctive truths which had been revealed to and through him. He would desire the Christians in Rome to have his own statement of the great doctrines of grace so bitterly assailed everywhere by legalistic teachers.

THEME: The theme of Romans is "the Gospel of God" (Rom 1:1), the very widest possible designation of the whole body of redemption truth, for it is He with whom is "no respect of persons"; and who is not "the God of the Jews only," but "of the Gentiles also"; Rom 2:11; Rom 3:29. Accordingly, "all the world" is found guilty Rom 3:19, and a redemption is revealed as wide as the need, upon the alone condition of faith. Not only does Romans embody in the fullest way the doctrines of grace in relation to salvation, but in three remarkable chapters (Romans 9-11.) the great promises to Israel are reconciled with the promises concerning the Gentiles, and the fulfilment of the former shown to await the completion of the church and coming of the Deliverer out of Zion Rom 11:25-27. The key-phrase is "the righteousness of God"; Rom 1:17; Rom 3:21; Rom 3:22.

The Epistle, exclusive of the introduction (Rom 1:1-17), is in seven parts.

1. The whole world guilty before God, Rom 1:18 to Rom 3:20.

2. Justification through the righteousness of God by faith, the Gospel remedy for guilt, Rom 3:21 to Rom 5:11.

3. Crucifixion with Christ, the resurrection life of Christ, and the walk in the Spirit, the Gospel provision for inherent sin, Rom 5:12 to Rom 8:13.

4. The full result in blessing of the Gospel, Rom 8:14-39.

5. Parenthesis: the Gospel does not abolish the covenant promises to Israel, Rom 9:1 to Rom 11:36.

6. Christian life and service, Romans 12:1-15:33. The outflow of Christian love, Romans 16:1-27.

footnotes.text: The Heb. and (Greek - ἀλεκτοροφωνία , safety, preservation, healing, and soundness). Salvation is the great inclusive word of the Gospel, gathering into itself all the redemptive acts and processes: as justification, redemption, grace, propitiation, imputation, forgiveness, sanctification, and glorification. Salvation is in three tenses: (1) The believer has been saved from the guilt and penalty of sin Luk 7:50; 1Co 1:18; 2Co 2:15; Eph 2:5; Eph 2:8; 2Ti 1:9 and is safe. (2) the believer is being saved from the habit and dominion of sin Rom 6:14; Php 1:19; Php 2:12; Php 2:13; 2Th 2:13; Rom 8:2; Gal 2:19; Gal 2:20; 2Co 3:18. (3) The believer is to be saved in the sense of entire conformity to Christ. Rom 13:11; Heb 10:36; 1Pe 1:5; 1Jn 3:2. Salvation is by grace through faith, is a free gift, and wholly without works; Rom 3:27; Rom 3:28; Rom 4:1-8; Rom 6:23; Eph 2:8. The divine order is: first salvation, then works; Eph 2:9; Eph 2:10; Tit 3:5-8.

footnotes.text: Lit. a propitiatory sacrifice, through faith by his blood; (Greek - ἱλαστήριον , "place of propitiation)." The word occurs, 1Jn 2:2; 1Jn 4:10 as the trans. of hilasmos, "that which propitiates," "a propitiatory sacrifice." Hilasterion is used by the Septuagint, and Heb 9:5 for "mercy-seat." The mercy-seat was sprinkled with atoning blood in the day of atonement Lev 16:14 in token that the righteous sentence of the law had been (typically) carried out, so that what must else have been a judgment-seat could righteously be a mercy-seat; Heb 9:11-15; Heb 4:14-16, a place of communion Exo 25:21; Exo 25:22. In fulfilment of the type, Christ is Himself the hilasmos, "that which propitiates," and the hilasterion, "the place of propitiation" --the mercy-seat sprinkled with His own blood-- the token that in our stead He so honoured the law by enduring its righteous sentence that God, who ever foresaw the cross, is vindicated in having "passed over" sins from Adam to Moses Rom 5:13 and the sins of believers under the old covenant (See Scofield " Exo 29:33 ") and just in justifying sinners under the covenant. There is no thought in propitiation of placating a vengeful God, but of doing right by His holy law and so making it possible for Him righteously to show mercy. remission passing over of sins done aforetime, i.e. since Adam. Cf. Heb 9:15.

Justification originates in grace; Rom 3:24; Tit 3:4; Tit 3:5 is through the redemptive and propitiatory work of Christ, who has vindicated the law; Rom 3:24; Rom 3:25; Rom 5:9 is by faith, not works; Rom 3:28-30; Rom 4:5; Rom 5:1; Gal 2:16; Gal 3:8; Gal 3:24 and may be defined as the judicial act of God whereby He justly declares righteous one who believes on Jesus Christ. It is the Judge Himself Rom 8:31-34 who thus declares. The justified believer has been in court, only to learn that nothing is laid to his charge. Rom 8:1; Rom 8:33; Rom 8:34.

footnotes.text: The passage (Rom 7:7-25) is autobiographical. Paul’s religious experience was in three strongly marked phases: (1) He was a godly Jew under the law. That the passage does not refer to that period is clear from his own explicit statements elsewhere. At that time he held himself to be "blameless" as concerned the law Php 3:6. He had "lived in all good conscience" Act 23:1. (2) With his conversion came new light upon the law itself. He now perceived it to be "spiritual" (Rom 7:14). He now saw that, so far from having kept it, he was condemned by it. He had supposed himself to be "alive," but now the commandment really "came" (Rom 7:9) and he "died." Just when the apostle passed through the experience of Rom 7:7-25 we are not told. Perhaps during the days of physical blindness at Damascus Act 9:9, perhaps in Arabia Gal 1:17. It is the experience of a renewed man, under the law, and still ignorant of the delivering power of the Holy Spirit Rom 8:2. (3) With the great revelations afterward embodied in Galatians and Romans, the apostle’s experience entered it third phase. He now knew himself to be "dead to the law by the body of Christ," and, in the power of the indwelling Spirit, "free from the law of sin and death" Rom 8:2 while "the righteousness of the law" was wrought in him (not by him) while he walked after the Spirit Rom 8:4, Romans 7. is the record of past conflicts and defeats experience as a renewed man under law. sin Sin. footnotes.text: The passage (Rom 7:7-25) is autobiographical. Paul’s religious experience was in three strongly marked phases: (1) He was a godly Jew under the law. That the passage does not refer to that period is clear from his own explicit statements elsewhere. At that time he held himself to be "blameless" as concerned the law Php 3:6. He had "lived in all good conscience" Act 23:1. (2) With his conversion came new light upon the law itself. He now perceived it to be "spiritual" (Rom 7:14). He now saw that, so far from having kept it, he was condemned by it. He had supposed himself to be "alive," but now the commandment really "came" (Rom 7:9) and he "died." Just when the apostle passed through the experience of Rom 7:7-25 we are not told. Perhaps during the days of physical blindness at Damascus Act 9:9, perhaps in Arabia Gal 1:17. It is the experience of a renewed man, under the law, and still ignorant of the delivering power of the Holy Spirit Rom 8:2. (3) With the great revelations afterward embodied in Galatians and Romans, the apostle’s experience entered it third phase. He now knew himself to be "dead to the law by the body of Christ," and, in the power of the indwelling Spirit, "free from the law of sin and death" Rom 8:2 while "the righteousness of the law" was wrought in him (not by him) while he walked after the Spirit Rom 8:4, Romans 7. is the record of past conflicts and defeats experience as a renewed man under law. sin Sin. footnotes.text: Remnant, Summary: In the history of Israel, a "remnant" may be discerned, a spiritual Israel within the national Israel. In Elijah’s time 7,000 had not bowed the knee to Baal 1Ki 19:18. In Isaiah’s time it was the "very small remnant" for whose sake God still forbore to destroy the nation Isa 1:9. During the captivities the remnant appears in Jews like Ezekiel, Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, Esther, and Mordecai. At the end of the 70 years of Babylonian captivity it was the remnant which returned under Ezra and Nehemiah. At the advent of our Lord, John the Baptist, Simeon, Anna, and "them that looked for redemption in Jerusalem" Luk 2:38 were the remnant. During the church-age the remnant is composed of believing Jews Rom 11:4; Rom 11:5. But the chief interest in the remnant is prophetic. During the great tribulation a remnant out of all Israel will turn to Jesus as Messiah, and will become His witnesses after the removal of the church Rev 7:3-8. Some of these will undergo martyrdom Rev 6:9-11 some will be spared to enter the millennial kingdom Zec 12:6 to Zec 13:9. Many of the Psalms express, prophetically, the joys and sorrows of the tribulation remnant. remnant Remnant. footnotes.text: Remnant, Summary: In the history of Israel, a "remnant" may be discerned, a spiritual Israel within the national Israel. In Elijah’s time 7,000 had not bowed the knee to Baal 1Ki 19:18. In Isaiah’s time it was the "very small remnant" for whose sake God still forbore to destroy the nation Isa 1:9. During the captivities the remnant appears in Jews like Ezekiel, Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, Esther, and Mordecai. At the end of the 70 years of Babylonian captivity it was the remnant which returned under Ezra and Nehemiah. At the advent of our Lord, John the Baptist, Simeon, Anna, and "them that looked for redemption in Jerusalem" Luk 2:38 were the remnant. During the church-age the remnant is composed of believing Jews Rom 11:4; Rom 11:5. But the chief interest in the remnant is prophetic. During the great tribulation a remnant out of all Israel will turn to Jesus as Messiah, and will become His witnesses after the removal of the church Rev 7:3-8. Some of these will undergo martyrdom Rev 6:9-11 some will be spared to enter the millennial kingdom Zec 12:6 to Zec 13:9. Many of the Psalms express, prophetically, the joys and sorrows of the tribulation remnant. remnant Remnant. See, Isa 1:9. grace Grace (in salvation). vs. 2Co 8:9; Rom 3:24 See note, (See Scofield " Joh 1:17 ") .

verses.text: For it is written, As I live, saith the Lord, every knee shall bow to me, and every tongue shall confess to God.
verses.marked_text: For it is written, As I live, saith the Lord, every knee shall bow to me, and every tongue shall confess to God.

verses.text: So then every one of us shall give account of himself to God.
verses.marked_text: So then every one of us shall give account of himself to God.

verses.text: Let us not therefore judge one another any more: but judge this rather, that no man put a stumblingblock or an occasion to fall in his brother’s way.
verses.marked_text: Let us not therefore judge one another any more: but judge this rather, that no man put a stumblingblock or an occasion to fall in his brother’s way.

verses.text: I know, and am persuaded by the Lord Jesus, that there is nothing unclean of itself: but to him that esteemeth any thing to be unclean, to him it is unclean.
verses.marked_text: I know, and am persuaded by the Lord Jesus, that there is nothing unclean of itself: but to him that esteemeth any thing to be unclean, to him it is unclean.

verses.text: But if thy brother be grieved with thy meat, now walkest thou not charitably. Destroy not him with thy meat, for whom Christ died.
verses.marked_text: But if thy brother be grieved with thy meat, now walkest thou not charitably. Destroy not him with thy meat, for whom Christ died.

verses.text: Let not then your good be evil spoken of:
verses.marked_text: Let not then your good be evil spoken of:

verses.text: For the kingdom of God is not meat and drink; but righteousness, and peace, and joy in the Holy Ghost.
verses.marked_text: For the kingdom<fn n="2"/> of God is not meat and drink; but righteousness, and peace, and joy in the Holy Ghost.

footnotes.text: See, Gal 4:9-11; Col 2:20-23. (See Scofield " Mat 6:33 ") . righteousness (See Scofield " Rom 10:10 ") .

verses.text: For he that in these things serveth Christ is acceptable to God, and approved of men.
verses.marked_text: For he that in these things serveth Christ is acceptable to God, and approved of men.

verses.text: Let us therefore follow after the things which make for peace, and things wherewith one may edify another.
verses.marked_text: Let us therefore follow after the things which make for peace, and things wherewith one may edify another.

verses.text: For meat destroy not the work of God. All things indeed are pure; but it is evil for that man who eateth with offence.
verses.marked_text: For meat destroy not the work of God. All things indeed are pure; but it is evil for that man who eateth with offence.

verses.text: It is good neither to eat flesh, nor to drink wine, nor any thing whereby thy brother stumbleth, or is offended, or is made weak.
verses.marked_text: It is good neither to eat flesh, nor to drink wine, nor any thing whereby thy brother stumbleth, or is offended, or is made weak.

verses.text: Hast thou faith? have it to thyself before God. Happy is he that condemneth not himself in that thing which he alloweth.
verses.marked_text: Hast thou faith? have it to thyself before God. Happy is he that condemneth not himself in that thing which he alloweth.

verses.text: And he that doubteth is damned if he eat, because he eateth not of faith: for whatsoever is not of faith is sin.
verses.marked_text: And he that doubteth is damned<fn n="3"/> if he eat, because he eateth not of faith: for whatsoever is not of faith is sin.

verses.text: Let every one of us please his neighbour for his good to edification.
verses.marked_text: Let every one of us please his neighbour for his good to edification.

verses.text: For even Christ pleased not himself; but, as it is written, The reproaches of them that reproached thee fell on me.
verses.marked_text: For even Christ pleased not himself; but, as it is written, The reproaches of them that reproached thee fell on me.

verses.text: For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.
verses.marked_text: For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.

verses.text: Now the God of patience and consolation grant you to be likeminded one toward another according to Christ Jesus:
verses.marked_text: Now the God of patience and consolation grant you to be likeminded one toward another according to Christ Jesus:

verses.text: That ye may with one mind and one mouth glorify God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.marked_text: That ye may with one mind and one mouth glorify God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.text: Wherefore receive ye one another, as Christ also received us to the glory of God.
verses.marked_text: Wherefore receive ye one another, as Christ also received us to the glory of God.

verses.text: Now I say that Jesus Christ was a minister of the circumcision for the truth of God, to confirm the promises made unto the fathers:
verses.marked_text: Now I say that Jesus Christ was a minister of the circumcision for the truth of God, to confirm the promises made unto the fathers:

verses.text: And that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy; as it is written, For this cause I will confess to thee among the Gentiles, and sing unto thy name.
verses.marked_text: And that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy; as it is written, For this cause I will confess to thee among the Gentiles, and sing unto thy name.

verses.text: And again he saith, Rejoice, ye Gentiles, with his people.
verses.marked_text: And again he saith, Rejoice, ye Gentiles, with his people.

verses.text: And again, Praise the Lord, all ye Gentiles; and laud him, all ye people.
verses.marked_text: And again, Praise the Lord<fn n="2"/>, all ye Gentiles; and laud him, all ye people.

verses.text: And again, Esaias saith, There shall be a root of Jesse, and he that shall rise to reign over the Gentiles; in him shall the Gentiles trust.
verses.marked_text: And again, Esaias saith, There shall be a root of Jesse, and he that shall rise to reign over the Gentiles; in him shall the Gentiles trust.

verses.text: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
verses.marked_text: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.

verses.text: And I myself also am persuaded of you, my brethren, that ye also are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to admonish one another.
verses.marked_text: And I myself also am persuaded of you, my brethren, that ye also are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to admonish one another.

verses.text: Nevertheless, brethren, I have written the more boldly unto you in some sort, as putting you in mind, because of the grace that is given to me of God,
verses.marked_text: Nevertheless, brethren, I have written the more boldly unto you in some sort, as putting you in mind, because of the grace<fn n="3"/> that is given to me of God,

verses.text: That I should be the minister of Jesus Christ to the Gentiles, ministering the gospel of God, that the offering up of the Gentiles might be acceptable, being sanctified by the Holy Ghost.
verses.marked_text: That I should be the minister of Jesus Christ to the Gentiles, ministering the gospel of God, that the offering up of the Gentiles might be acceptable, being sanctified by the Holy Ghost.

verses.text: I have therefore whereof I may glory through Jesus Christ in those things which pertain to God.
verses.marked_text: I have therefore whereof I may glory through Jesus Christ in those things which pertain to God.

verses.text: For I will not dare to speak of any of those things which Christ hath not wrought by me, to make the Gentiles obedient, by word and deed,
verses.marked_text: For I will not dare to speak of any of those things which Christ hath not wrought by me, to make the Gentiles obedient, by word and deed,

verses.text: Through mighty signs and wonders, by the power of the Spirit of God; so that from Jerusalem, and round about unto Illyricum, I have fully preached the gospel of Christ.
verses.marked_text: Through mighty signs and wonders, by the power of the Spirit of God; so that from Jerusalem, and round about unto Illyricum, I have fully preached the gospel of Christ.

verses.text: Yea, so have I strived to preach the gospel, not where Christ was named, lest I should build upon another man’s foundation:
verses.marked_text: Yea, so have I strived to preach the gospel, not where Christ was named, lest I should build upon another man’s foundation:

verses.text: But as it is written, To whom he was not spoken of, they shall see: and they that have not heard shall understand.
verses.marked_text: But as it is written, To whom he was not spoken of, they shall see: and they that have not heard shall understand.

verses.text: For which cause also I have been much hindered from coming to you.
verses.marked_text: For which cause also I have been much hindered from coming to you.

verses.text: But now having no more place in these parts, and having a great desire these many years to come unto you;
verses.marked_text: But now having no more place in these parts, and having a great desire these many years to come unto you;

verses.text: Whensoever I take my journey into Spain, I will come to you: for I trust to see you in my journey, and to be brought on my way thitherward by you, if first I be somewhat filled with your company.
verses.marked_text: Whensoever I take my journey into Spain, I will come to you: for I trust to see you in my journey, and to be brought on my way thitherward by you, if first I be somewhat filled with your company.

verses.text: But now I go unto Jerusalem to minister unto the saints.
verses.marked_text: But now I go unto Jerusalem to minister unto the saints.

verses.text: For it hath pleased them of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor saints which are at Jerusalem.
verses.marked_text: For it hath pleased them of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor saints which are at Jerusalem.

verses.text: It hath pleased them verily; and their debtors they are. For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, their duty is also to minister unto them in carnal things.
verses.marked_text: It hath pleased them verily; and their debtors they are. For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, their duty is also to minister unto them in carnal things.

verses.text: When therefore I have performed this, and have sealed to them this fruit, I will come by you into Spain.
verses.marked_text: When therefore I have performed this, and have sealed to them this fruit, I will come by you into Spain.

verses.text: And I am sure that, when I come unto you, I shall come in the fulness of the blessing of the gospel of Christ.
verses.marked_text: And I am sure that, when I come unto you, I shall come in the fulness of the blessing of the gospel of Christ.

verses.text: Now I beseech you, brethren, for the Lord Jesus Christ’s sake, and for the love of the Spirit, that ye strive together with me in your prayers to God for me;
verses.marked_text: Now I beseech you, brethren, for the Lord Jesus Christ’s sake, and for the love of the Spirit, that ye strive together with me in your prayers to God for me;

verses.text: That I may be delivered from them that do not believe in Judea; and that my service which I have for Jerusalem may be accepted of the saints;
verses.marked_text: That I may be delivered from them that do not believe in Judea; and that my service which I have for Jerusalem may be accepted of the saints;

verses.text: That I may come unto you with joy by the will of God, and may with you be refreshed.
verses.marked_text: That I may come unto you with joy<fn n="4"/> by the will of God, and may with you be refreshed.

verses.text: Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen.
verses.marked_text: Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen.

verses.text: I commend unto you Phebe our sister, which is a servant of the church which is at Cenchrea:
verses.marked_text: I commend unto you Phebe our sister, which is a servant of the church which is at Cenchrea:

verses.text: That ye receive her in the Lord, as becometh saints, and that ye assist her in whatsoever business she hath need of you: for she hath been a succourer of many, and of myself also.
verses.marked_text: That ye receive her in the Lord, as becometh saints, and that ye assist her in whatsoever business she hath need of you: for she hath been a succourer of many, and of myself also.

verses.text: Greet Priscilla and Aquila my helpers in Christ Jesus:
verses.marked_text: Greet Priscilla and Aquila my helpers in Christ Jesus:

verses.text: Who have for my life laid down their own necks: unto whom not only I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles.
verses.marked_text: Who have for my life laid down their own necks: unto whom not only I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles.

verses.text: Likewise greet the church that is in their house. Salute my wellbeloved Epenetus, who is the firstfruits of Achaia unto Christ.
verses.marked_text: Likewise greet the church that is in their house. Salute my wellbeloved Epenetus, who is the firstfruits of Achaia unto Christ.

verses.text: Greet Mary, who bestowed much labour on us.
verses.marked_text: Greet Mary, who bestowed much labour on us.

verses.text: Salute Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen, and my fellowprisoners, who are of note among the apostles, who also were in Christ before me.
verses.marked_text: Salute Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen, and my fellowprisoners, who are of note among the apostles, who also were in Christ before me.

verses.text: Greet Amplias my beloved in the Lord.
verses.marked_text: Greet Amplias my beloved in the Lord.

verses.text: Salute Urbane, our helper in Christ, and Stachys my beloved.
verses.marked_text: Salute Urbane, our helper in Christ, and Stachys my beloved.

verses.text: Salute Apelles approved in Christ. Salute them which are of Aristobulus’ household.
verses.marked_text: Salute Apelles approved in Christ. Salute them which are of Aristobulus’ household.

verses.text: Salute Herodion my kinsman. Greet them that be of the household of Narcissus, which are in the Lord.
verses.marked_text: Salute Herodion my kinsman. Greet them that be of the household of Narcissus, which are in the Lord.

verses.text: Salute Tryphena and Tryphosa, who labour in the Lord. Salute the beloved Persis, which laboured much in the Lord.
verses.marked_text: Salute Tryphena and Tryphosa, who labour in the Lord. Salute the beloved Persis, which laboured much in the Lord.

verses.text: Salute Rufus chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.
verses.marked_text: Salute Rufus chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.

verses.text: Salute Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, and the brethren which are with them.
verses.marked_text: Salute Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, and the brethren which are with them.

verses.text: Salute Philologus, and Julia, Nereus, and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints which are with them.
verses.marked_text: Salute Philologus, and Julia, Nereus, and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints which are with them.

verses.text: Salute one another with an holy kiss. The churches of Christ salute you.
verses.marked_text: Salute one another with an holy kiss. The churches of Christ salute you.

verses.text: Now I beseech you, brethren, mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned; and avoid them.
verses.marked_text: Now I beseech you, brethren, mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned; and avoid them.

verses.text: For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly; and by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.
verses.marked_text: For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly; and by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.

verses.text: For your obedience is come abroad unto all men. I am glad therefore on your behalf: but yet I would have you wise unto that which is good, and simple concerning evil.
verses.marked_text: For your obedience is come abroad unto all men. I am glad therefore on your behalf: but yet I would have you wise unto that which is good, and simple concerning evil.

verses.text: And the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.
verses.marked_text: And the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.

verses.text: Timotheus my workfellow, and Lucius, and Jason, and Sosipater, my kinsmen, salute you.
verses.marked_text: Timotheus my workfellow, and Lucius, and Jason, and Sosipater, my kinsmen, salute you.

verses.text: I Tertius, who wrote this epistle, salute you in the Lord.
verses.marked_text: I Tertius, who wrote this epistle, salute you in the Lord.

verses.text: Gaius mine host, and of the whole church, saluteth you. Erastus the chamberlain of the city saluteth you, and Quartus a brother.
verses.marked_text: Gaius mine host, and of the whole church, saluteth you. Erastus the chamberlain of the city saluteth you, and Quartus a brother.

verses.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
verses.marked_text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
